name: Seeking Strahad
summary: Carendin Halgar sends Horde warlocks across the Great Sea to seek Strahad Farsan. Above Ratchet, a human sorcerer offers a path beyond basic shadowcraft toward the difficult art of summoning a felhunter.

sections.title: A Master Across the Sea
sections.body: Carendin Halgar, a Forsaken warlock trainer in the Undercity's Magic Quarter, knows when an initiate has outgrown basic instruction. He sends his pupils beyond Lordaeron's ruins to find Strahad Farsan. Halgar warns that Strahad is a living human, but no weakling, and says not to treat him as an enemy. For warlocks, the pursuit of demonic mastery often crosses racial and factional lines.

sections.title: The Overlook at Ratchet
sections.body: Strahad works from the bluffs above Ratchet, the goblin port in the Barrens. Near a stone watchtower, he looks down on the sailors, mercenaries, and merchants below, whose blissful ignorance of the Twisting Nether amuses him. Horde warlocks who reach him may bring distrust and simmering hatred in their eyes. Strahad accepts that raw malice as fuel to shape into dark authority.

faq.q: Why is an Undercity warlock sending me to a human?
faq.answer: Warlocks often set aside factional divisions to pursue rare and potent dark lore. Carendin Halgar says Strahad Farsan has a specialized command of greater demonic summonings that Halgar cannot teach. In the pursuit of demonic power, an instructor's knowledge matters more than their bloodline.

faq.q: Where exactly is Strahad Farsan located?
faq.answer: Strahad Farsan is in the Barrens, on the high cliffs above the goblin port of Ratchet. He stands near a stone tower overlooking the bay and the busy harbor docks.

faq.q: What kind of power does Strahad teach?
faq.answer: Strahad guides experienced warlocks through the complex rituals for binding greater demons from the Twisting Nether. His instruction leads toward the dangerous trials of summoning and commanding a felhunter.

faq.q: Is Strahad allied with the Alliance?
faq.answer: Though human, Strahad works from neutral goblin territory in Ratchet and is unaffiliated with the Grand Alliance. He is an independent practitioner who deals freely with Horde and Alliance warlocks able to endure his instruction.

When you arrive, Strahad tests your resolve and enlists you to recover the scattered fragments and components of the Tome of the Cabal. The search ranges far as you seek the ritual for summoning a felhunter.

faq.q: Why does Strahad welcome hatred in his students?
faq.answer: Demonic magic feeds on intense emotion, dominance, and willpower. Hatred can be focused and disciplined, helping a summoner bind chaotic beings from the Nether before they consume someone who lacks discipline.

angles.text: As a warlock, this marks a rite of passage around your thirtieth circle of power. You leave minor imp and voidwalker bindings behind as you turn toward command of the predatory felhunter.
As a Horde warlock, you set aside your usual hostility toward humans and travel to neutral Ratchet to learn from a living sorcerer.
As an Undead, you are among the Forsaken disciples Carendin Halgar sends from the Undercity. His choice shows that even Sylvanas's loyalists use living masters to expand their arsenal.
